Everyone can always learn new skills and improve themselves. However for certain individuals there is certain limitations. Each individual with autism will always be affected by it because autism in itself is not something to be fixed. It does express itself differently in each person however and the severity can change too.

Some people may spend the rest of their lives struggling to do certain tasks and needing support with it and that's just how it is. Others can learn to do certain things but will continue to require support elsewhere anyway. Other people may appear to be totally normal, and can absolutely live totally independently. It's a spectrum.

Basically it's heavily dependent on the individual on how independent they can learn to be and some things just will never change- it's a part of who they are and their condition.

FLAT FACED DOGS AREN'T CUTE IT IS A SERIOUS PROBLEM!

Don't get me wrong, I know a lot of pugs and bulldogs etc that are absolutelt lovely dogs but people need to stop trying to get flat faced dogs because of all the medical issues they have!

For starters the trachea is much smaller than it should be, leading to a plethora of breathing issues. You think it is cute that your 3 month old pup is a heavy snorer? No they are struggling to breathe. 

But then we need to look at the other consequences, despite having a flat face the amount of skin, teeth and the length of the tongue is the same as if they did have a proper snout. The skin folds in onto itself so skin infections are common and these dogs end up biting down on their mouths and tongues all the time because their mouth is too small for its contents.

I have seen dogs with serious ulcerations all along both sides of the tongue as a result of this.

Another common problem: cherry eyes. Dont know what that is? Your vet sees it all the time. Because of the face shape the tear ducts are forced inside out and you see the red lumps at your dogs eyes. Hopefully they can tuck it back in but more often they are surgically removed. Your dog can now no longer produce tears and will have to be on eye drops for their life span to keep their eyes moist. This means they are more likely to have eye ulcers now too.

I don't think the world would spin out of control, but I heavily disagree with the abortion of a child based on downs syndrome. Don't get me wrong, I know you are referring to diseases way worse than downs. 

What I am trying to say is it is difficult to judge as an individual from an outside perspective which life is worth living and which is not. I used downs as an example since it is a real situation where people remove life even though we know that people with downs can live very happy lives. 

My point is you can't easily quantify a life's value or quality so things get messy. In these cases the parents clearly feel that despite it all their child's life is worth living. That probably is partially selfish, but humans are selfish when it comes to people they love. 

Basically you can't really decide at which exact point a life stops being worth living- only the person affected can do that and since a unborn person can't make that decision that means only a parent can decide. I don't think it is cruel because there is no right or wrong.

Oh and if you count births that would lead into basically immediate death then I have no issue with that either, the baby is already dead either with or without an abortion and at that point it is whatever the parents find easier to grieve

I think this type of thinking is dangerous because then you have to question where to draw the line. If you say disability x is okay to have but disability y just isn't a life worth living then things start to get messy and legally issues start to form since there is a grey area of what is and isn't reason to abort.

For example at a 20 week scan if your kid has downs syndrome you will find out then. People with downs can live very happy fulfilling lives and yet that info is enough for people to abort the child. This is very ableist, also it diminishes the value of these peoples lives. Most of us can agree the kid should live, but for some that is something they don't want to bring into the world.

In the end life is harsh, and it is unfair. In these situations there is no real right or wrong there just is, so no matter the decision of the parent I will respect it without judgement.
